errors.expected: Chest pocket fills 40-80% of the frame, framed tight on the left chest pocket
errors.actual: Pocket spans 36% of frame width / 34% of frame height; framing is a chest-and-collar crop rather than a tight pocket crop

errors.description: The drawing shows both pocket side edges vertical and parallel. In the photograph the left edge is vertical but the right edge slopes inward by roughly 8% of the pocket width from top to bottom, so the patch reads as a slight trapezoid. Consistent with the body curving toward the armhole rather than a construction error, but it is a departure from the drawn outline.
errors.expected: Both side edges vertical and parallel, as drawn
errors.actual: Right side edge slopes inward ~8% of pocket width top-to-bottom; left edge vertical

errors.description: The two chamfers are near-symmetric but not identical: left chamfer horizontal run measures ~11.5% of pocket width, right ~12.2%, and the right chamfer starts marginally lower.
errors.actual: Left/right chamfer runs differ by roughly 0.7% of pocket width

lockedFeatures: six-sided outline: flat bottom edge with two chamfered lower corners (the defining hexagon-pocket geometry)
chamfer horizontal run measured at ~11.5% of pocket width, matching the drawing's ~11.7%
chamfer angle approximately 45 degrees, as drawn
top hem / facing seam runs straight across at ~19% of pocket height from the top edge (drawing: ~18%)
edge stitching present around the full pocket perimeter
pocket height-to-width ratio ~1.2, matching the drawing
single patch pocket on the wearer's left chest, positioned to the pocket side of the button placket exactly as drawn
real photograph on a male model, white cotton poplin, no line-art or CGI look
no annotation, dimension line, arrow, label or red guide mark traced from the drawing
no generic-category substitution: reads unmistakably as the hexagon pocket, clearly distinct from the round and triangle siblings in this same group
notes: Attempt 3 of 3, graded against public/images/pocket/hexagon-pocket.jpg magnified 6x. Best result in the shirt-pocket::pocket group. The defining six-sided geometry is reproduced accurately - chamfer run measured 11.5% of pocket width against the drawing's 11.7%, and the flat bottom edge between the chamfers is present. Attempt 3 is clearly better than attempt 2, whose chamfers were far too long and read closer to a shallow point than a hexagon. All shortfalls are minor and none touch the showcased feature.
